title: Flat, finitely presented, separated, quasi-finite morphisms are finite locally free on a stratification (Stacks 07RZ)
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] which is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite]. Then there exist closed subsets $\emptyset=Z_{-1}\subseteq Z_0\subseteq Z_1\subseteq Z_2\subseteq\cdots\subseteq S$ such that, with $S_r=Z_r\setminus Z_{r-1}$ ($r\geq0$), the sets $S_r$ are pairwise disjoint with union $S=\coprod_{r\ge0}S_r$, and this stratification has the following universal property: for every morphism of schemes $g:T\to S$, the projection $X\times_ST\to T$ (fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product]) is finite locally free of degree $r$ [def-pc-finite-locally-free] if and only if $g(T)\subseteq S_r$ (as sets). Moreover, each inclusion $S_r\to S$ is quasi-compact, i.e. $S_r\cap W$ is quasi-compact for every quasi-compact open $W\subseteq S$. (Stacks Project, More on Morphisms, Lemma Tag 07RZ.)
